title: Lytic or lysogenic?
caption: In the lytic cycle the virus replicates at once and the cell bursts. In the lysogenic cycle the viral DNA joins the host chromosome as a prophage and is copied with it, hiding for generations until something triggers the lytic cycle.
alt: A flow chart: if the viral DNA does not integrate into the host chromosome, the cycle is lytic and the cell bursts; if it integrates as a prophage, the cycle is lysogenic, and may later become lytic.
description: Does the viral genome integrate into the host chromosome? If not, it replicates immediately and the cell bursts: the lytic cycle.
If it does, it is a prophage: it is copied with the host DNA every time the cell divides, and later may switch to the lytic cycle: the lysogenic cycle.

q1.q: Does the viral genome integrate into the host chromosome?

lyso.outcome: Lysogenic: the genome is a prophage, copied with the host DNA, and later may become lytic

lytic.outcome: Lytic: the virus replicates immediately and the cell bursts
